patches.reason: ProgressBar builds its gauge's HTML across statements: m starts as an opening <font color='blue'>, the step i+1 closes it and opens <font color='white'>, and the end closes that. Message markup spans cannot cross statements, so each piece settles on its own and the gauge would show 30 blocks without its colours (before, it showed the colour tags as text). The loop now collects the blue and the white blocks first and one expression writes each colour around its blocks; the text shown without the gauge is one blue text too.

theEdger and its go, stop and cum scripts declare PicCodeBChars without a value and set it to PicCodeB.toCharArray() before each use, but a script call such as getImage or save comes between the set and the reads, so the conversion cannot keep the variable known as not null and every read stopped the package from compiling. PicCodeBChars starts as the characters of empty text instead, a value no use ever reads, so nothing shown or stored changes.

The picture-watching part reads the online lists of pictures and players, pads them to their full length with "0" and "", and then converts every player code with PlCodeCode[i] as Integer, which fails on a padded "". Legacy reached that only when the server's lists were shorter than their full length; the conversion keeps the online values in the package's storage (SX_ONLINE_STORAGE), where the lists start empty, so watching always stopped. An empty player code now reads as 0, the code of no player.
